anomalies.obs: On the Power Control sheet, U38 (SN74LVC1G07 open‑drain buffer) has its input pin 1 (A) tied directly to GND while the control signal 3.3V_5V_PI_CONTROL is applied to pin 2 (/OE). Its pin 4 (Y) drives the gate node of the 5V_switched load switch (Q15/Q3) through R32 to +5V.
anomalies.exp: For this part to act as a /OE‑controlled sink (the topology used elsewhere on the same drawing, e.g. U5 with pin1=A tied to +3V3 and pin2=/OE driven by NET0068), the input A must be held HIGH (tied to VCC, 3.3V_PI_OUT) so that a low on /OE makes Y sink. With A tied to GND the open‑drain output never conducts, so the 5V_switched enable path cannot turn on.

evidence.quote: Power Control sheet: U38 pin2 = 3.3V_5V_PI_CONTROL, pin1 = GND, pin4 -> R32/+5V and Q15/Q3 gates
LED Enable sheet: U5 pin1 = +3V3 (via R72), pin2 = NET0068 — correct /OE‑sink wiring for comparison
This board provides motor control communication to four Odrive motor controllers ... motor power control

anomalies.impact: The 5V_switched rail (which feeds the external +3V3 LDO U4, the WS2812 VCCB and other 5V loads) can never be enabled by 3.3V_5V_PI_CONTROL, so those downstream rails stay off regardless of CM4 GPIO state.

parsed.summary: The drawing shows U38, an SN74LVC1G07 used to sink the 5V_switched load‑switch gate, wired with its input (A, pin 1) tied to GND and the control on /OE — the opposite of the working /OE‑sink arrangement used by U5 on the same sheet — so the buffer can never sink and the switched 5V rail cannot be enabled. This is a wiring deviation not covered by the spec's documented open issues.
